lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Nehemiah: overview
nodes.d: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, prays and returns to Jerusalem to rebuild its wall in fifty-two days despite opposition (chs. 1-7), then the law is read, the feast of booths is kept, the people confess and covenant (chs. 8-10), and the city is repopulated, the wall dedicated and abuses corrected (chs. 11-13).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Nehemiah, from the prayer in Susa to the reforms at the end?
ev: Name the main parts: building the wall, reading the law and covenant, dedication and reforms
Say who Nehemiah was and what he did for Jerusalem

nodes.t: Nehemiah hears about Jerusalem and prays
nodes.d: Nehemiah, in Shushan in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, hears from Hanani that the remnant in Judah is in affliction and Jerusalem's wall is broken down; he weeps, fasts and prays, confessing sin, recalling the LORD's word to Moses about scattering and gathering, and asks for mercy before the king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah responded when he heard about Jerusalem and what he prayed?
ev: Say what Nehemiah learned and how he responded (1:3-4)
Say what promise to Moses he recalls (1:8-9)

nodes.t: The king grants Nehemiah's request
nodes.d: Months later Nehemiah, as cupbearer, is asked by Artaxerxes why he is sad; after a quick prayer he asks to be sent to rebuild Jerusalem, and the king grants letters and timber, the good hand of God being on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Nehemiah got permission to go to Jerusalem?
ev: Say what Nehemiah did before answering the king (2:4)
Say what the king gave him (2:7-9)

nodes.t: Nehemiah inspects the wall and rallies the people
nodes.d: After three days in Jerusalem Nehemiah rides out by night to view the broken wall, then tells the officials of God's good hand and the king's words, and the people say, Let us rise up and build; Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem mock them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah got the people ready to build the wall?
ev: Say what Nehemiah did first and why he did it by night (2:12-15)
Say how the people and the enemies responded (2:18-19)

nodes.t: Who built the wall
nodes.d: Chapter 3 names the priests, families, officials and guilds who repaired each section and gate of Jerusalem's wall, from the Sheep Gate around to the Sheep Gate again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Nehemiah 3 lists so many builders?
ev: Name the first gate mentioned and the people who built it (3:1)
Say how the work was shared

nodes.t: Opposition and a weapon in every builder's hand
nodes.d: Sanballat and Tobiah mock the builders; Nehemiah prays and sets a guard when they plot to attack, tells the people to remember the LORD and fight for their families, and from then half the men work and half hold spears, each builder with a sword, trusting that God will fight for them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the builders kept working while their enemies threatened them?
ev: Say how Nehemiah responded to mockery and threat (4:4, 9, 14)
Describe how the work went on under threat (4:16-18)

nodes.t: Nehemiah stops oppression among the Jews
nodes.d: The poor cry out that they have mortgaged lands and sold children into bondage to their own brethren during a famine; Nehemiah rebukes the nobles for exacting usury and they promise to restore what was taken, while he reports that he and his brethren did not take the governor's food allowance because of the fear of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong when the nobles took usury and what Nehemiah did?
ev: Say what the poor complained of (5:2-5)
Say why Nehemiah did not take the governor's bread (5:14-15)

nodes.t: Plots against Nehemiah and the wall is finished
nodes.d: Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem try to lure Nehemiah away, send an open letter accusing him of rebellion, and hire Shemaiah to frighten him into the temple; Nehemiah refuses, prays, and the wall is finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul in fifty-two days, so that the nations' confidence fails because the work was of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah resisted his enemies' schemes and how the wall was finished?
ev: Say what Nehemiah answered when invited to meet (6:3)
Say how long the wall took and what the enemies concluded (6:15-16)

nodes.t: Guarding Jerusalem and the register of the first returnees
nodes.d: With the wall built and doors set up, Nehemiah puts Hanani and Hananiah in charge of Jerusalem and sets watches at the gates; the city is large but its people few, so God puts it in Nehemiah's heart to gather the people by genealogy, and he finds the register of those who came up first, which is read out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Nehemiah looked for the register of the first returnees?
ev: Say who was put in charge and how the gates were guarded (7:1-3)
Say what record Nehemiah found (7:5)

nodes.t: Ezra reads the law and the people weep
nodes.d: On the first day of the seventh month all the people gather at the water gate; Ezra reads the law from morning until midday, the Levites explain it so the people understand, and when they weep Nehemiah, Ezra and the Levites tell them to rejoice because the joy of the LORD is their strength.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when Ezra read the book of the law to the people?
ev: Describe how the law was read and explained (8:3-8)
Say what the leaders told the people when they wept (8:9-10)

nodes.t: The feast of booths is kept
nodes.d: On the second day the leaders study the law and find that Israel should dwell in booths in the seventh month; the people make booths of branches and keep the feast with very great gladness, as had not been done since the days of Joshua, with daily reading from the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the people kept the feast of booths in Nehemiah's day?
ev: Say what the law said about the feast (8:14-15)
Say how long they kept the feast and what they heard (8:17-18)

nodes.t: The people fast and confess
nodes.d: On the twenty-fourth day Israel assembles with fasting, sackcloth and earth, separates from foreigners, stands and confesses their sins and their fathers' iniquities, reads the law a quarter of the day and worships; the Levites call on them to bless the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Israel gathered to confess their sins in Nehemiah 9?
ev: Say how the people showed their repentance (9:1-2)
Say how the time was spent (9:3)

nodes.t: The Levites' prayer retelling Israel's story
nodes.d: The prayer blesses the LORD as creator, recalls his choice of Abram and his covenant to give the land to his seed, the exodus, Sinai, manna and water, the golden calf, the conquest, the cycle of rebellion and rescue under judges, the prophets' warnings, and ends by asking for mercy in their present distress; the people write a sure covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Israel's history as told in the Levites' prayer and say what it asks for?
ev: Find the lines about the covenant with Abraham (9:7-8)
Say how the prayer describes God's patience and the people's repeated rebellion (9:16-31)

nodes.t: The sure covenant is sealed
nodes.d: The leaders, priests and Levites seal the covenant, and the rest of the people swear to walk in God's law, to avoid intermarriage with the peoples of the land, to keep the sabbath and seventh year, and to support the temple with a yearly charge, wood, firstfruits and tithes, saying "we will not forsake the house of our God".
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the people promised in the covenant in Nehemiah 10?
ev: List some commitments the people made (10:28-39)
Say what they promised about the house of God (10:39)

nodes.t: Who lived in Jerusalem
nodes.d: The rulers dwell in Jerusalem and the people cast lots so that one in ten will live there, and the people bless those who volunteer; the chapter lists the Judah and Benjamin families, priests, Levites and others in Jerusalem and the towns elsewhere.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jerusalem was filled with people after the wall was built?
ev: Say how people were chosen to live in Jerusalem (11:1-2)
Say who was among the residents

nodes.t: Priests and Levites from Zerubbabel's time
nodes.d: Chapter 12:1-26 lists the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua and their successors, noting Jeshua, Joiakim, Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua as the line of high priests, and the Levites chief of the fathers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Nehemiah 12:1-26 records?
ev: Name some priests who went up with Zerubbabel (12:1-7)
Say what the list records about later priests (12:10-11, 22-23)

nodes.t: The dedication of the wall
nodes.d: The Levites are sought out to keep the dedication with gladness and singing; Nehemiah brings the princes up on the wall and appoints two great thanksgiving companies that go in procession and meet at the house of God, where great sacrifices are offered and the joy of Jerusalem is heard afar off, and the services and storehouses are organised.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated?
ev: Describe the two companies on the wall (12:31-40)
Say what was heard afar off (12:43)

nodes.t: Separation from foreigners and Tobiah's chamber
nodes.d: When the book of Moses is read, the people separate the mixed multitude after finding that Ammonites and Moabites were not to enter the congregation; on a later return from the king Nehemiah finds that Eliashib gave Tobiah a chamber in the temple and he throws Tobiah's goods out, cleanses the chamber, and restores the Levites' portions.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Nehemiah did about Tobiah's room in the temple?
ev: Say what the law said that led to the separation (13:1-3)
Say what Nehemiah did about Tobiah and the Levites (13:7-13)

nodes.t: Sabbath breaking and mixed marriages
nodes.d: Nehemiah rebukes the nobles for trading on the sabbath, orders the gates shut at sunset, and warns the merchants; he also contends with Jews who married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, citing Solomon's sin, and drives away a son of the high priest who was son-in-law to Sanballat. He ends by asking God to remember him for good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Nehemiah dealt with the sabbath and with mixed marriages?
ev: Say what Nehemiah did to guard the sabbath (13:19-22)
Say what example he used against mixed marriages (13:26)

nodes.t: Ezra: overview
nodes.d: Ezra reports the return from Babylon under Cyrus and Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the temple despite opposition (chs. 1-6), then Ezra's own journey to Jerusalem, his prayer over intermarriage, and the people's covenant to put away foreign wives (chs. 7-10).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Ezra, from Cyrus's decree to the people's confession?
ev: Name the two parts: the return and temple under Zerubbabel, and Ezra's mission
Say how the book begins (Cyrus) and ends (the list of those with foreign wives)

nodes.t: The list of those who returned
nodes.d: Chapter 2 lists those who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua by family and town, then priests, Levites, singers, porters and temple servants, notes some who could not prove their ancestry, and gives the total and the freewill gifts for the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra records the names and numbers of the returnees?
ev: Say who led the group (2:2)
Say what some of the chief fathers gave (2:68-69)

nodes.t: Esther: overview
nodes.d: Esther tells how a Jewish orphan becomes queen of Persia, Haman plots to destroy the Jews, Esther and Mordecai act, the plot is reversed, and the feast of Purim is established. The name of God does not appear in the book.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Esther from Vashti's removal to the feast of Purim?
ev: Say who the main people are: Ahasuerus, Esther, Mordecai and Haman
Say what the feast of Purim remembers
